items.title: Mike Vax interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 29, 2022
items.q: especially with John Von Ohlen and John Worster that we talked about different charts

ctx.x: Is there a discussion that would have happened back then when you became the lead player, did you ever discuss things off the bandstand with the drummer and the bass player about, you know we’re not hanging together on this. Or is it just something that has to happen while you’re playing?

I think it’s a bit of both. I don’t think — the responsibility of the lead trumpet player is that you have to make sure things are going because in a professional situation if things aren’t happening in the band there are times when the leader is going to blame the lead trumpet player. You know? And yeah there are times, especially with John Von Ohlen and John Worster that we talked about different charts and it wasn’t like John was saying well Vax you’re not coming in right, or I was saying well you’re not…

A number of Basie alums have talked about how the Count was sort of a hands off — he didn’t say anything unless something was really bad. And I wondered if Stan was like that or was he more hands-on and how did he deal with any, I guess I’ll call them discipline issues?
